summary: In Greek mythology, Stichius (Ancient Greek Στιχίος) was a leader of the brazen-coated Boeotians at Troy. Hector slays him with Arcesilaus when Apollo sends panic upon the Argives at the ships (Iliad 15.329–331). Distinct from the Athenian Stichius who fights beside Menestheus in Book 13.

sections.heading: Boeotian leader
paragraphs: Homer's death-notice is explicit: Hector laid low Stichius and Arcesilaus — "the one a leader of the brazen-coated Boeotians, and the other a trusty comrade of great-souled Menestheus." Stichius here is the Boeotian; Arcesilaus is Menestheus' comrade.

The Catalogue places the Boeotian contingent under Peneleos, Leitus, Arcesilaus, Prothoënor, and Clonius; Stichius appears only at his death, as a named Boeotian captain in the rout at the hollow ships.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: Not stichius-athenian, the Athenian who with Menestheus carries Amphimachus and later follows among the picked Athenians (Iliad 13). Wikipedia's stub merges the two under one Athenian biography; the atlas keeps the Homeric split.
